title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 86
paragraphs: Such is the manner of fighting of these men, and they were arrayed next to the Persians. The Medes had the same equipment as their infantry, and the Cissians likewise. The Indians were armed in the same way as their foot soldiers, and they both rode horses and drove chariots drawn by horses or wild asses. The Bactrians were equipped as their infantry were, and the Caspians likewise. The Libyans too were equipped as their infantry, and all of them drove chariots. So too the Caspians and the Paricanians had equipment like their infantry, and they all rode on camels, which were no slower than horses.
